expects.rule: A starting price is published: for weddings the lowest package with its hours of coverage, for portraits the session fee and the cheapest print or product.
The work fills the first screen: real commissioned images, edited to a tight selection, grouped by story, client or genre.
Where the photographer is based and how far they travel is stated near the top.
One enquiry route on every page (check your date, get in touch) leading to a short form that asks the date, place and budget.
What is delivered is described: hours of coverage, number of images, delivery time, albums or prints, usage rights for commercial work.
Proof from clients is real: named testimonials, client or press logos, published features.

traits: 8 of 8 sites read state where the photographer is based (France, Bologna, Italy with destinations, Vancouver, Belgium, Seoul, Puerto Rico with a local time stamp).
0 of 8 show a price on the home page; Tatiana Braoun lists three packages by hours and media without price, Elina Kustlyvy asks for a budget range in the form.
Navigation is short: 2 items (Taras Yareha, Gregor Collienne), 3 (Adovasio, Elina Kustlyvy), 4 (Tatiana Braoun); only Siempreric and OFF-BEAT have deep menus.

4 of 8 have an on-site enquiry route (Tatiana 'Check your date' popup, Adovasio 'Check availability', Daniele & Marilia 'Book now' form, Elina form with budget ranges); 3 rely on a bare email link (Gregor Collienne, OFF-BEAT, Siempreric).
4 of 4 wedding sites read lead with weddings shown as couples' stories (named galleries on Adovasio, 'Real weddings' on Tatiana, Stories on Daniele & Marilia, a photo stack on Taras).

Type does the branding while the images stay neutral: white #ffffff and black with one muted green #435b45 (Tatiana Braoun, Satoshi with Cormorant), greys #bdbdbd (Adovasio), Hatton serif on #fafafa (Elina Kustlyvy), Neue Haas Grotesk on #101010 (Siempreric).

sites.name: Tatiana Braoun
sites.why: Destination wedding photographer based in France: label 'wedding photography', headline 'For lovers who feel deeply', 'Based in France & worldwide', a SEE REAL WEDDINGS link, a 'Now taking booking for 2026 | 2027' block with a CHECK YOUR DATE popup form, and three packages described by hours and media (35 mm, 120 mm film, drone) without prices. White with muted green #435b45, Satoshi with Cormorant italics. Cookie banner defaults to off.

sites.name: Adovasio
sites.why: Wedding photography studio in Italy (title names Tuscany, Lake Como, Amalfi Coast): headline 'Weddings that never fade', one line on an editorial, Italian approach, a Check availability button, then a grid of couples' galleries named by first names. Three-item nav (Portfolio, About, Contact), closing line 'Reach out to see if your date is available'. Greys #bdbdbd with a terracotta #c17957. No prices.
sites.recognition: Awwwards Site of the Day, 2026-03-05 (also Developer Award)

sites.name: Daniele & Marilia
sites.why: Wedding photographer duo in Italy: three-line headline 'Insatiable, impactful & intentional', a Book now button in the top bar, a 'Featured on' row (Vogue, Brides, Harper's Bazaar), a numbered menu (Portfolio, Stories, Photobook), a 'Passport to Photography' list of destinations by month, and an enquiry form under 'Invest in the indelible'. No prices. Some headline letters render doubled in the page text.

sites.name: Taras Yareha
sites.why: Wedding photographer in Bologna: name, 'Wedding Photographer' and the city, then a stack of about 18 wedding photographs, some black and white, with no button on the first screen. Two-item nav (Works, Contact). Nothing else competes with the pictures; prices, travel area and an enquiry form are not on the home page.

sites.name: Elina Kustlyvy
sites.why: Product photographer in Vancouver working with brands in Los Angeles, Seattle and Toronto: the name and that sentence as headline, email and Instagram, a row of product shots (skincare, cosmetics, nail polish), services by kind (beauty, skincare, e-commerce), recent projects, five named client testimonials, and a form written as sentences ('My name is', 'The brand I am looking to photograph is') with budget ranges $1,500-3,000 to $8,000+. Hatton serif on #fafafa.

sites.name: Gregor Collienne
sites.why: Portrait and commercial photographer in Belgium: 'Welcome.' and two sentences (based in Belgium, portraits, fine art, storytelling, available wherever the project is), a Contact Me button that opens an email, then a grid of about 140 thumbnails with a grid/list toggle, each linking to its project. Two-item nav (Overview, Work). No form, prices or client names.

sites.name: Studio OFF-BEAT
sites.why: Portrait studio in Seoul, Korean and English side by side: headline 'Life shifts in OFF-BEAT moments, we capture that rhythm before it fades', two header photographs, then three work areas (Portrait, Project for brands such as 29CM x NIKE, Stage for performances), each with a View All link. Contact by studio email and Instagram; no prices, hours, address or booking. Off-white #fafafa and #0a0a0a with a red #d92d20.

sites.name: Siempreric
sites.why: Eric Rojas, photographer and director from San Juan: 'PHOTOGRAPHER & DIRECTOR', a local time stamp (PR, AST), a light/dark switch and a list/grid toggle, a portrait as the first image, and the work grouped into Commissions, campaigns (adidas, Crocs x Young Miko, Medalla) and concert tours, plus tearsheets. Contact is a protected email link. Neue Haas Grotesk on #101010 and #f5f5f5.

sites.name: Avagyan Wedding Photography
sites.why: Wedding photographer Noro Avagyan in Italy, page titled 'Wedding Photographer in Italy'; the gallery listing describes an elegant, editorial approach. The page renders in a script only, so the layout, enquiry route and prices could not be read; its stylesheet is black, white and grey #c8c8c8. (not seen beyond the gallery listing)

avoid: No price at all, not even a starting price, so every enquiry starts with 'how much?'.
A contact route that is only a bare or protected email address, with no form asking for date, place and budget.
Hundreds of unedited thumbnails instead of a tight selection grouped by story or client.
Loading counters and intro animations that hold the pictures back on phone.
Stock or AI images, or other photographers' work, mixed into the portfolio.
No word on where the photographer works or whether they travel.
Menus and headings that render broken in text (doubled letters, placeholder labels).

sources.name: Format Magazine, Why portrait and wedding photography websites need a pricing page
